analogous

/uh-NAL-uh-guhs/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Analogous means similar in a way that lets two genuinely different things be compared, so that one can be understood through the other.

Critics noted that a film director's job is analogous to an orchestra conductor's: each shapes dozens of performers into a single vision.

Example

To explain the new circuit, the engineer said electric current is analogous to water flowing through pipes, with voltage acting like water pressure.

Analogous flags a structured comparison: current maps onto water, voltage onto pressure. The two systems are genuinely different, but the pattern of one explains the other.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

comparable: Comparable means similar enough to be set side by side and measured — two prices, two test scores, two apartments. Analogous claims more: the things are genuinely different in kind, yet their structures line up so you can reason from one to the other. Comparable items share a scale; analogous systems mirror each other.

parallel: Parallel describes things that run alongside each other in matching form — two careers, two plotlines unfolding the same way. Analogous goes beyond matching shape: it says one thing's workings can explain the other's. Parallel lives merely resemble each other; analogous systems let you reason from one to the other.

akin: Akin means related or similar in nature — a loose family resemblance between things. Analogous is tighter and more structured: the two things must line up well enough that one can be understood through the other. Akin notes kinship; analogous licenses a working, point-by-point comparison.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

dissimilar: not alike

contrasting: strikingly different when set side by side

Where it sits · how tightly one maps onto the other — similar → analogous → identical

similar vs. analogous: Two things can be loosely similar; call them analogous only when the match is tight enough to reason from one to the other.

identical vs. analogous: Analogous systems mirror each other point by point; identical ones are the very same in every respect.

The pieces

Prefix — ana-

Prefix — ana-: according to, in proportion - Greek

Root — log-

Root — log-: word, reason, ratio - Greek logos

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: having the quality of - adjective-forming, from Latin -osus

Put it together

Put it together: 'In proportion, according to the same reasoning' - two things are analogous when the same pattern of reasoning maps one onto the other.

Word Choice

Formal; frequent in scientific, legal, and academic prose

Analogous almost always appears in the frame 'X is analogous to Y,' and it claims more than loose similarity: the two things must line up well enough to reason from one to the other. The related noun analogy names the comparison itself - situations are analogous; the comparison you draw between them is an analogy.
